title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election in Florida's 21st Congressional District
description: The 2026 general election for Florida's 21st Congressional District will determine who represents the Treasure Coast and northern Palm Beach County in the U.S. House. Incumbent Republican Brian Mast, first elected in 2016 and currently chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, is seeking re-election. The Democratic primary features Coast Guard veteran and former White House national security advisor James Martin and firefighter/paramedic Bernard Taylor, with the winner advancing to face Mast in November. The district leans Republican but became marginally more competitive under a 2026 redistricting map approved by the state legislature.

candidates.name: Brian Mast
candidates.summary: Brian Mast is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Florida's 21st Congressional District, first elected in 2016 and currently serving as Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. A U.S. Army veteran who lost both legs while serving as a bomb disposal technician in Afghanistan, Mast was awarded the Bronze Star and Purple Heart. He is running for re-election on a platform emphasizing national security, clean water, tax cuts, and conservative values.

candidates.name: James Martin
candidates.summary: James Martin is a fourth-generation Floridian, U.S. Coast Guard veteran, and former White House national security advisor running for Congress. He served as commanding officer of Coast Guard Cutter Ibis, served on four ships from the Arabian Gulf to the Eastern Pacific, and most recently served as Executive Secretary in the Office of the Vice President. His campaign focuses on lowering the cost of living, clean water restoration, anti-corruption reforms, healthcare access, and immigration reform.

candidates.name: Bernard Taylor
candidates.summary: Bernard Taylor is a fourth-generation Floridian, EMT/Paramedic, and firefighter running for Congress in Florida's 21st District. With years of experience as a first responder on the Treasure Coast, he is running on a platform of affordable healthcare, quality education, economic growth, and clean water. Taylor has emphasized grassroots fundraising and has pledged not to accept money from AIPAC.

forecast.rationale: No polling data exists for this race. The forecast relies entirely on structural factors: incumbent Brian Mast has held the seat since 2016, serves as Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee (substantial name-recognition and fundraising advantages), and the district leans Republican overall. The 2026 redistricting made the district marginally more competitive, but not enough to offset Mast's incumbency. Democrats face a contested primary between James Martin and Bernard Taylor with no clear frontrunner evident in the data, and no public polling or comparative fundraising data is available to gauge challenger strength. These factors point to a clear Republican advantage (consistent with a 'likely_r' rating at ~84% probability), but the complete absence of polling data keeps confidence low.
